title: You’re not struggling with sin.
paragraphs:
Because the most dangerous place a soul can live…
is not rebellion that feels wrong—

There are things you once felt convicted about…
that no longer bother you.

Conversations you entertain.
Screens you hide.
Thoughts you justify.
Habits you renamed so they sound harmless.
Sin didn’t kick the door in.
It made deals with your comfort.
Until one day, you stopped fighting.
And here’s the truth most people don’t say out loud:
When the fear of the Lord fades… sin stops feeling serious.
But because your vision of God did.

Proverbs 9:10 says,
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and the knowledge of the Holy One is insight.”
Meaning—if there is no reverence, no weight, no holy awareness of who God is…

You start calling darkness “manageable.”
You start calling compromise “growth.”
You start calling distance “peace.”
Some scholars interpret “fear” here not as terror, but as deep reverence, awe, and submission before a holy God.
Because when you truly see God as He is—holy, pure, blazing with righteousness—
you don’t flirt with what He died to destroy.
You don’t make peace with what nailed Christ to the cross.
Not because you’re trying to earn love—
but because you’ve seen His worth.

Ecclesiastes 12:13 says,
“Fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole duty of man.”

Same struggle.
Same secret.
Same cycle.
Now shame is louder than conviction.
And instead of running to God—

You pray less.
You hide more.
You scroll longer.
You numb deeper.
“If I really saw how holy God is… He wouldn’t want me anymore.”
Because that’s not the full story.
that same holy God made a way for sinners to come close.

Romans 5:8 says,
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
Not when you finally became consistent.
Jesus didn’t die for a polished version of you.
He died for the version of you that you’re trying to hide.
the fear of the Lord is no longer about running away.
It’s about finally seeing the cost of your sin…
and the depth of His mercy.

2 Corinthians 7:10 says,
“For godly grief produces a repentance that leads to salvation without regret, whereas worldly grief produces death.”
There are two kinds of sorrow.
One says, “I messed up, I’m worthless.”
The other says, “I messed up… I need Jesus.”
That’s the fear of the Lord.
Not fear that pushes you into darkness—
but fear that pulls you into surrender.

God sees everything…
and still made a way…
you don’t need a better version of yourself.
You don’t need more discipline first.
You don’t need to hide until you feel worthy.
You need to come to Jesus while you’re not.
Because He is not waiting for your perfection.
He is calling for your surrender.
Turn from what you’ve been excusing.

1 John 1:9 says,
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”
Will you keep managing your sin—
or will you finally surrender it?
If God is speaking to you right now…
And if this stirred something deep inside you…
